findings.description: SUBJECT-MATTER GAP (strongest). Spec says only 'tax-adjusted figures'. The code's Tax surface is a tax-LIABILITY model: per-accrual lifecycle rows keyed by (sale_id, lot_id, jurisdiction, tax_year) plus a per-(Jurisdiction, TaxYear) reserve summary carrying accrued/moved/paid/outstanding/shortfall from tax::annual_report. The spec text names none of: accruals, reserves, jurisdictions, tax years, lifecycle states. Consequence measured on both sides: all 3 A-runs independently built a completely different table (per-tax-lot adjusted basis, proceeds, realized/unrealized gain, Short/Long term, wash-sale disallowance) — A1 explicitly flags the ambiguity ('after-tax valuations vs tax-basis-adjusted lots') and picks the wrong branch; and all 3 B-runs had to invent SHEET-TAX-00x clauses naming the accrual/reserve entities because no spec text covers them. Zero column overlap between what the spec forces and what the code pins.

Two-band structure and exact names, unstated. Spec says 'The Tax tab' (singular). Code pins TWO ViewTabs from one render call: TAX_TAB = "Tax" and TAX_RESERVE_TAB = "Tax · Reserve Summary" (U+00B7 middle dot), with the reserve band deliberately NOT a fifth VIEW_TABS entry — VIEW_TABS is exactly [Positions, Open Lots, Realized, Tax], length 4, asserted in tabs.rs (`assert_eq!(VIEW_TABS.len(), 4)`) and `assert_ne!(tax.reserve_summary.name, tax.accruals.name)`. All 3 B-runs reconstructed this as their SHEET-TAX-001; no A-run produced a second band.

Exact column vocabularies, unstated. TAX_HEADER = [Sale ID, Lot ID, Jurisdiction, Tax Year, Amount, Lifecycle State]; TAX_RESERVE_HEADER = [Jurisdiction, Tax Year, Accrued, Moved, Paid, Outstanding, Shortfall]. Tests pin row width to header width (`assert_eq!(row.len(), tax.accruals.header.len())`, `assert_eq!(row.len(), TAX_RESERVE_HEADER.len())`) and pin the reserve header identity byte-for-byte. Spec states no columns at all. 3/3 B-runs recovered both headers verbatim.

Money rendering rule, unstated. fmt_cents pins: leading '-' iff negative, then |cents|/100, '.', |cents|%100 zero-padded to exactly 2 digits — no thousands separator, no currency symbol (Cents(5000) → "50.00"). formula.rs re-implements this exact formatter inline and asserts every one of the five reserve columns equals it (`assert_eq!(fed_row[rcol("Moved")].text(), "50.00")`). Spec says only that money is integer Cents.

Absent-amount and never-blank semantics, unstated. `a.applied_cents.map(fmt_cents).unwrap_or_default()` makes a missing accrual amount the EMPTY STRING — not "0.00", not a placeholder, not an error. Conversely the five reserve figures are never optional and formula.rs asserts none is empty ('None of the five is an empty string (the gap the review flagged)'). Spec is silent on missing values in both directions; all 3 B-runs surfaced the asymmetry, and A1/A3 guessed blank-vs-zero for a different column set entirely.

Label vocabularies, unstated. jurisdiction_label emits exactly "Federal" or "State({code})"; lifecycle_label emits exactly one of "Accrued"/"Allocated"/"Moved"/"Paid" with the AccrualState payload fields discarded (`AccrualState::Allocated { .. }` etc.); tax_year renders as raw integer digits. Spec states none of these string forms. 3/3 B-runs pinned them, including the payload-elision.

'No among-data summary rows' rule — enforced by code, absent from spec, and actively violated by the spec-side. tabs.rs asserts for every accrual row: column 0 non-empty, `assert_ne!(first, "RESERVE SUMMARY")`, and that no row equals TAX_RESERVE_HEADER embedded as data — the stated purpose being that the range stays natively filterable/sortable. The spec never states this. Direct evidence of the cost: all 3 A-runs appended an in-band totals row (A1 `Row::total_of(&rows)`, A2 `totals(&view.rows)`, A3 `push_totals` plus a trailing short/long row) and A1/A2/A3 all prepend a banner row — every one of those would fail `tax_accrual_band_has_no_among_data_summary_rows`.

'as-of-last-sync' is spec text with NO representation in the code. TaxView, both ViewTabs, and render_tax's signature carry no timestamp, no sync sequence, no freshness field — render_tax(&[Accrual], &[AnnualRow]) takes no clock or stamp at all. The only 'last sync' string in the crate is the FAILURE banner `"STALE — last sync {stale_banner_quote_ts}"`, written only when batch_update_view errors. No test pins as-of-ness. All 3 A-runs required an as_of/SyncStamp on the input struct and rendered it (A3 also carries the event-log seq); all 3 B-runs could only restate 'as-of-last-sync' as 'no live formula', and they got even that phrase from the crate's doc prose (lib.rs line 695 and the formula.rs comment echo the EARS wording verbatim) rather than from any enforced behavior. The property is doc-only, not pinned.

'stacked' is an undefined term in the spec that neither side can ground. A-side: all 3 runs read it as lot-stack ordering ('per-tax-lot rows in kernel order', 'disposal order preserved verbatim, the view never sorts'). Code-side: the only ordering behavior is verbatim iteration over the input slices (`for a in accruals`, `for r in annual_rows`), pinned only as count equality (`tax.accruals.rows.len() == accruals.len()`, `tax.reserve_summary.rows.len() == annual.len()`) plus a zip-order comparison — no test pins any stacking or sort rule, and nothing in the code distinguishes 'stacked' from 'input order'. The word does no work in either direction.

Crate-boundary and totality semantics, unstated. render_tax is total — returns TaxView unconditionally with no Result, no error path, and empty accrual or annual-row inputs are legal (contrast render_positions, which returns Result and can fail DuplicateSymbolRow). It also performs zero arithmetic on the reserve figures: outstanding and shortfall are copied verbatim from AnnualRow rather than derived (no netting, no re-summing, no cross-band reconciliation). Spec's 'kernel-exact' gestures at this boundary but never states it; 2/3 B-runs (B1 SHEET-TAX-009, B3 SHEET-TAX-009) made it an explicit clause.

Placement and publish mechanics, unstated. Tax is fourth in workbook_tab_order() — after Positions/Open Lots/Realized, strictly before History, then the three config tabs, then the two event-log tabs — and the order is reasserted idempotently on every republish (tabs.rs republishes twice and asserts both orders equal). Data rows are written from DATA_START_ROW = 2 beneath a frozen row-1 header that is written once and never rewritten, with the residual tail truncated. Spec states no placement or republish semantics. B1/B3 pinned all of it; B2 pinned DATA_START_ROW and the VIEW_TABS position.

The comparison term itself — 'the Positions live estimate' — is heavily pinned in code while the spec leaves it a bare noun phrase. Code: Est. Tax Rate is a VALUE from fmt_ppm rendering Ppm as {ppm/10000}.{ppm%10000:04}% (Ppm(150_000) → "15.0000%"), written as a userEnteredValue so Sheets coerces it to the numeric fraction in [0,1]; Est. Unrealized Tax (est) = =G{r}*H{r} and Net Unrealized (est) = =G{r}*(1-H{r}), row-anchored to r = index + DATA_START_ROW and tested never to leak another data row's number; an absent effective rate renders empty and degrades the post-tax columns to pre-tax. Only 1/3 B-runs (B2 SHEET-TAX-006/007) reconstructed this half, so agreement here is low — but formula.rs devotes three tests to it, so the code-side surplus is real.

notes:
Classification is BD-DRIFT rather than B-ONLY-DRIFT because the two directions converge on one root cause: SHEET-FORMULA-004 states a PROPERTY of the Tax tab (kernel-exact, not live) but never states its SUBJECT. That single omission produces surplus on both sides — the code fills the vacuum with an entire accrual+reserve domain model (finding 1, plus the header/format/label findings 2-6), and the spec-side runs fill the same vacuum with a different domain (lot-level basis/gain/wash-sale) whose natural shape (totals rows, banner rows) the code's tests actively forbid (finding 7).

On A/B asymmetry: the property the spec DOES state is the one part the code honors well — every Tax cell is Cell::Value, asserted by tax_tab_is_kernel_exact_not_live_formula over both bands. That is why B-side surplus dominates by count. But the A-side is not empty: 'as-of-last-sync' (finding 8) has literally zero representation in the code — render_tax takes no stamp — and 'stacked' (finding 9) is inert in both directions. Both are spec-traced, not A-side inventions, so they qualify as findings.

Assumption artifacts EXCLUDED as non-findings (unanimous A-side, no spec basis): the provenance banner row itself, in-view totals rows, the i128/saturating totals accumulator, MicroShares scale choice, wash-sale/term columns, and the 'never synced' empty-state behavior. Notably these are not merely unfounded — the banner and totals rows would fail the real tests, which is itself the evidence for finding 7 rather than a finding in its own right.

Stability: A-runs agree on essentially everything material (literal Cents not formulas; kernel owns all tax math; as-of banner; lot-level rows; totals row appended; empty input renders rather than errors) — high. B-runs: B1 and B3 are near-identical (10 clauses each, same content, same ordering); B2 covers the same Tax-band clauses but spends two clauses reconstructing the Positions live-estimate side instead of the ordering/totality clauses. Core Tax-surface agreement is 3/3 on findings 2-6; the divergence is coverage breadth, not contradiction — high, with the caveat that finding 12 rests on a single run.
